claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 begins cooling from a high-temperature single-phase disordered BCC state.
A moderate cooling rate permits sufficient local atomic diffusion in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Local diffusion during moderate cooling produces short-range compositional ordering.
Al segregation is a particularly important contributor to the proposed short-range compositional ordering.
Short-range compositional ordering and compositional fluctuations establish nucleation sites for ordered intermetallic phases.
Moderate cooling therefore promotes formation of ordered intermetallic phases from the initially disordered BCC matrix.
Rapid quenching suppresses diffusion-driven elemental segregation.
Suppressing segregation by rapid quenching locks in a predominantly disordered BCC structure.
Under identical subsequent thermal exposure, moderately cooled samples will contain more ordered-phase material than rapidly quenched controls.
Rapidly quenched controls will remain predominantly disordered and will not develop significant ordered-phase fractions.
Ordered-phase formation can be detected and compared using diffraction and microscopy.
The proposed mechanism should apply only when cooling permits moderate atomic diffusion without complete homogenization.
The proposed ordering pathway should not apply under extremely rapid cooling because diffusion is suppressed.
The proposed mechanism may not apply when the starting phase is not BCC.
The critical cooling rate for activating the proposed pathway is unknown.
The quantitative contribution of each segregating element, including Al, is unknown.

Failure to observe a statistically significant increase in either ordered-phase formation or short-range compositional ordering after moderate cooling relative to rapid quenching would falsify the hypothesis.
